subject: Workaround for shared libraries problems on Linux

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Workaround for shared libraries problems on Linux
parts:
The testing version for 64bit contains now also libR as a shared library, to host the new feature that you can pass also R-code to define a model component. We have been testing this new feature, and it seems to be stable and I will send out a separate email about that in due time. for the curious ones: see inla.doc("rgeneric")    and    demo(rgeneric) 

As a consequence of this, is that we had to switch to using dynamic builds, passing also dynamic libraries with the code. For some, older, Linux systems, this creates problems and you'll get an error starting up the inlaprogram. Usually this is solvable for the linux-skilled ones, by editing

> INLA:::inla.call.builtin()
[1] "/home/hrue/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.run"


but as a workaround, I have added also the static build versions for Linux from testing-version

 INLA 0.0-1458745824, dated 2016-03-23 (15:54:25+0100).

and beyond. 

To enable the static builds instead, do 

library(INLA)
d = dirname(INLA:::inla.call.builtin())
inla.setOption(inla.call = paste(d,"/inla.static", sep=""))
inla.setOption(fmesher.call = paste(d,"/fmesher.static", sep=""))


then you should get something similar to :

> inla.getOption("inla.call")
[1] "/home/hrue/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.static"
> inla.getOption("fmesher.call")
[1] "/home/hrue/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher.static"

and you're read to go

Best,
H
